- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overreacts — dampen forecast growth and favor lower end of range.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility — if sentiment swings sharply, align forecast slope with sentiment direction, not historical trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trend — use 18-day history as anchor, not 30-day trend, to avoid over-optimism in short-term forecasts.
